question: What is the primary function of a Health Maintenance Organisation in healthcare financing?
explanation: HMOs collect periodic prepayments to pool financial risks so that healthcare costs are distributed across a larger population. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h1)

question: Why are HMOs considered vital for reducing out-of-pocket spending in Nigeria?

options.A: They eliminate all administrative costs in private clinics
options.B: They provide care upfront in exchange for pre-collected periodic premiums
options.C: They offer free medical services to every citizen without registration
options.D: They replace government funding entirely with private donations

explanation: Prepayment models protect patients from paying cash directly at the point of service during medical emergencies. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h1)

question: What is the primary role of a designated primary care provider within an HMO network?

options.B: Auditing financial records of tertiary hospitals
options.C: Acting as the initial point of contact and care gatekeeper
options.D: Regulating federal health insurance licensing laws

explanation: Primary care providers manage routine health issues and control referrals to higher levels of specialized care. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h2)

question: A patient enrolled in an HMO goes directly to a tertiary specialist without seeing their primary doctor first. What will likely happen?

options.A: The tertiary hospital will pay the patient a cash refund
options.B: The HMO may refuse to cover the cost of the specialist visit
options.C: The government will absorb the specialist billing charges
options.D: The primary provider will automatically lose their operating license

explanation: Managed care structures require formal referrals from primary providers before secondary or tertiary services are covered. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h2)

question: What defines the capitation payment method used by HMOs?

options.A: Reimbursement based on daily hospital bed occupancy
options.B: An hourly wage paid directly to administrative staff
options.C: A fixed regular amount paid per registered enrollee
options.D: Payment made only when a patient undergoes surgery

explanation: Capitation involves paying providers a set fee per patient over a specific period, regardless of service utilization. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h3)

question: How does capitation affect the financial risk distribution between the HMO and the provider?

options.A: It ensures the patient carries the burden of paying hospital staff
options.B: It places all financial responsibility squarely back on the federal government
options.C: It eliminates all financial risks for every party involved in care
options.D: It transfers some financial risk from the HMO to the primary provider

explanation: If an enrolled patient falls sick frequently, the provider still receives the same fixed capitation amount, absorbing the extra cost. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h3)

question: Which body is officially responsible for regulating and accrediting HMOs in Nigeria?

options.B: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.C: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NHIA sets operational guidelines, accredits health maintenance organizations, and protects insurance enrollees. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h4)

question: Why does the regulatory body enforce strict capital reserve requirements for HMOs?

options.A: To collect direct taxes for state infrastructural development
options.B: To ensure doctors earn higher salaries than administrative officers
options.C: To guarantee they can pay medical bills and avoid sudden insolvency
options.D: To prevent private hospitals from owning insurance companies

explanation: Adequate financial reserves ensure an HMO can fulfill its financial obligations to healthcare providers during high-claim periods. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h4)

question: What is a common complaint reported by enrollees regarding some Nigerian HMOs?

options.A: Unexpected out-of-pocket demands at hospitals due to delayed payments
options.B: Overabundance of specialist doctors at rural primary posts
options.C: Excessive reimbursement rates given to primary health clinics
options.D: Mandatory enrollment in foreign medical tourism programs

explanation: When HMOs delay paying accredited hospitals, facilities sometimes illegally demand cash payments directly from enrollees. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h5)

question: How do rising inflation and drug costs negatively impact capitation-based agreements?

options.A: The regulatory agency dissolves all active private health insurance policies
options.B: Fixed capitation payments lose purchasing power, making patient care unprofitable for providers
options.C: HMOs automatically increase enrollee salaries to match market prices
options.D: Hospitals immediately stop admitting patients who require expensive drugs

explanation: When the cost of medical supplies rises faster than fixed capitation fees, healthcare facilities struggle to provide adequate care without losing money. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h5)

question: What is a key administrative task nurses perform for patients under HMO cover?

options.A: Calculating annual corporate profits for the insurance firm
options.B: Auditing government treasury funds allocated for healthcare
options.C: Verifying insurance status and processing pre-authorizations
options.D: Setting national capitation tariffs for medical procedures

explanation: Nurses often check eligibility and handle documentation required by HMOs before carrying out specific diagnostic tests or treatments. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h6)

question: A patient needs an urgent specialized scan, but the HMO pre-authorization code is delayed. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately without notifying the attending physician
options.B: Cancel all further medical treatments until the insurance contract expires
options.C: Pay for the expensive medical scan using personal nursing salary funds
options.D: Advocate for the patient while liaising with the hospital HMO desk for expedited approval

explanation: Nurses act as patient advocates, communicating with administrative staff to resolve authorization delays without compromising clinical care. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h6)
